clue.text: Dismiss contract

definitions.meaning: in cricket a fielder can get a batter out by holding the ball in the air
to pick up an illness, as in coming down with a cold

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard verbs: one from cricket fielding, one from getting an infection.

clue.text: One inside to invite scorn

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is someone inside prison
to tempt is to invite or entice

explanation.surface: A prisoner trying to provoke derision.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is disdain or derision, a straight synonym of scorn.

clue.text: US magazine published in period off work

parts.note: Time is a weekly American news magazine
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: An American magazine issued during a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is also the name of a listings magazine, which fits the surface nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A break from work or activity, an idiomatic phrase for a pause or rest.

clue.text: Rustic old tramp

parts.note: hob is an old word for a country fellow or yokel

explanation.surface: An elderly country vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a vagrant or itinerant worker, the same as a tramp.

clue.text: A quiet lecturer in break getting hand

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play softly

indicators.note: the word in places the lecturer within the break

parts.note: a pause is a short break

explanation.surface: A softly spoken teacher, pausing mid-lecture, gets a round of clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a big hand means clapping for them, so hand is idiom for acclaim by clapping.

clue.text: Sense nitpicker deployed?

indicators.note: deployed suggests the letters of sense nitpicker are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Is this the faculty a fault-finder uses?
explanation.definitionFit: Fussy attention to trivial detail is exactly what a nitpicker brings, so the whole clue describes the trait.

clue.text: Scottish landscape feature is close reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for close is spoken, giving a Scottish word

parts.note: to lock a door is to close it securely

explanation.surface: A Highland scene said to be near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like the adjective 'near' but is the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake or sea inlet in Scotland, such as Ness, is a typical Scottish geographic feature.

clue.text: A learner trailing students in two universities? That's odd

indicators.note: in places the students within the two universities

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, so two of them give U and U
the NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK student body
L is for learner, as on British L-plates for new drivers

explanation.surface: A beginner lagging behind students at two colleges: strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailing' puts A and L after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary is strange or odd, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Athletic competition like two triathlons principally

parts.note: two is an even number, so even describes what two is like

indicators.note: principally means taking the leading letter of triathlons

explanation.surface: A sporting contest resembling a pair of multi-sport races.
explanation.definitionFit: A single contest in an athletics meeting, such as the high jump, is one item on the programme.

clue.text: Theatrical employee taking charge on very hot day carrying decoration

parts.note: a ward is someone in another's charge

indicators.note: carrying means the hot day holds the decoration inside it

parts.note: a roaster is a scorchingly hot day
the BEM is the British Empire Medal, an honour

explanation.surface: A stagehand put in charge on a sweltering day while wearing a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre company this person looks after the costumes, a backstage job title.

clue.text: Dictator promoting new prejudice mostly in African country

indicators.note: promoting moves the letter for new up to the front of the dictator's name

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: bias is prejudice

explanation.surface: A tyrant pushing a fresh bigotry within an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves the N of AMIN to the front, giving NAMI; 'mostly' trims BIAS to BIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a nation on Africa's south-west coast, an example of the category.

clue.text: Withdrawn figure in park by lake before exercise

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park
L is the map abbreviation for lake
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A shy person in a park near a lake, about to work out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or loner keeps away from society, so a withdrawn figure is a person living in seclusion.

clue.text: God near house on a regular basis

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words near house, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A deity living close to someone's home, as a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love, counterpart of Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Allow master in entrance of mine

indicators.note: in puts the master's letter within the mine entrance

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: Letting a boss into the mouth of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in or permit something, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Absolutely impartial magistrate ditching formality

indicators.note: ditching means the formality is thrown out of the magistrate's title

parts.note: a justice, such as a justice of the peace, is a fair-minded magistrate
ice is stiff reserve or formality, as in breaking the ice

explanation.surface: A totally fair judge dropping the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impartial' looks like part of the definition, but it belongs to the magistrate; 'ditching' removes ICE from JUSTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means exactly or absolutely, as in just perfect or just right.

clue.text: Unnerve Arab ruler in audience

indicators.note: in audience means as heard by listeners, so the ruler's title is spoken

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief or ruler

explanation.surface: Rattling an emir who is granting an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'audience' with a ruler is a formal meeting, but here it means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle or disturb someone's composure, as in shaken by the news.

clue.text: Hot dish made from scratch

definitions.meaning: a spicy dish of Indian origin
to rub down or scrape a horse's coat with a comb is an old verb sense

explanation.surface: A spicy meal cooked with no ready-made ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from scratch' reads as a cooking idiom; split it, and scratch is a grooming verb, as in a curry-comb.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a spiced dish; the verb means to groom or rub down a horse with a comb.

clue.text: Piece of ground 50 in labour left as cover for retirement

parts.note: a patch is a small plot of land
work is labour

indicators.note: in sets the fifty within the word for left

parts.note: quit means left, as in quit the job
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A smallholding, fifty people working, and leaving it all behind on retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but here it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread made of sewn squares covers you when you retire for the night.

clue.text: Marked individual at home in capital in middle of cold

indicators.note: the second in places all that within the middle of cold
middle of takes the central letters of cold
the first in puts the home word within the capital

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A distinctive person staying home in a capital city in midwinter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marked individual' reads as someone singled out, but it means an eccentric; 'at home' is the crossword convention IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or one-of-a-kind character is called a real one, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Risk cab averted, manoeuvring for unreliable motorist?

indicators.note: manoeuvring suggests moving the letters of risk cab averted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A taxi accident narrowly avoided by some clever steering.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who gives unwanted directions is a pseudo-motorist; the question mark flags this whimsical, unreliable kind.

clue.text: Foreign character in a slum disturbed old boy

indicators.note: in places the Greek letter within the rearranged letters
disturbed suggests the letters of a slum are stirred into a new order

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A stranger in a run-down district upset a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A former student of a school or college, which is what old boy means in Britain.

clue.text: Meat put in oven is onus

indicators.note: put in means the answer sits inside the run of letters oven is onus

explanation.surface: Getting the joint into the oven is someone's duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer flesh eaten as food is a type of game meat.

clue.text: Grim condo urgently blocked

indicators.note: blocked means held within the run of letters condo urgently

explanation.surface: A bleak report that an apartment was hastily sealed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern and gloomy in manner is a close synonym of grim.

clue.text: Diamonds — what about part, inmost part?

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: about means the word for what goes round the part

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what

explanation.surface: A jeweller asking what part of the stones matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: The deepest or innermost area, as in the depths of the forest.

clue.text: Dim pretence, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for pretence is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a feint is a sham move, a pretence

explanation.surface: A weak pretext, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim light or sound is weak or hard to perceive, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Problem produced by decline around November

indicators.note: around puts the decline word round the letter for November

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A difficulty caused by a slump in late autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch or drawback is a snag, a common synonym for a problem.

clue.text: A finalist literally among poor grades producing bewilderment

indicators.note: among places A and the final letter between the poor grades

parts.note: D and E are low marks in a grading scheme
the letter that literally finishes the alphabet is Z

explanation.surface: A competitor in the final, stuck between bad marks, is left reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of confusion or stupefaction, a direct synonym for bewilderment.

clue.text: Retain fare

definitions.meaning: to continue to possess something rather than give it up
food and lodging, as in earning one's board

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to go on possessing; the noun means food and maintenance, a sense of fare.

clue.text: Long to import complete ornament

indicators.note: to import means the longing word brings the complete word inside it

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
to end something is to complete it

explanation.surface: Yearning to buy in a finished decorative piece from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging piece of jewellery worn on a chain is a kind of ornament.

clue.text: Patron, maybe, with exotic tones in headwear

parts.note: a patron saint is one example of a saint, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: exotic suggests the word tones is made strange and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sponsor in a strangely coloured hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat, a specific type of headwear.

clue.text: Shortly straying around Eastern drinking establishment

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters round the letter for Eastern
straying suggests the letters of shortly wander out of order

explanation.surface: Wandering briefly round an Oriental pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' rearranges SHORTLY to HOSTLRY, and 'around' wraps that round E.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or pub, an old-fashioned word for a place serving drinks.

clue.text: Parking on country road put back as a punishment?

definitions.note: an adjective meaning serving to punish; the phrase stands in for it loosely, as the question mark admits

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

indicators.note: put back means the country road is written backwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow rural road

explanation.surface: A parking ticket on a rural lane, reversed as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal describes measures intended to punish, as in penal servitude.
